newsitem.title: USA: Clinton outraged at killing of British soldier.
newsitem.headline: Clinton outraged at killing of British soldier.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday condemned the "callous" killing of a British soldier by a suspected IRA gunman and urged pro-British loyalists in Northern Ireland to show restraint.
The 23-year-old soldier was manning a checkpoint outside the village of Bessbrook in Northern Ireland when he was hit by a shot from a high velocity rifle on Wednesday night.

"I am grieved and outraged by the callous killing of a British soldier in Northern Ireland yesterday," Clinton said in a written statement. "The first lady and I extend our deepest sympathy to the soldier's family and to the British government and people on the loss of this young man."

There was no immediate claim of responsibility but the British and Irish governments quickly blamed the Irish Republican Army, which is fighting to oust Britain and reunite the province with the rest of Ireland.

"All those who care about the future of Northern Ireland must join me in condemning this cowardly crime," Clinton said. "I remain convinced that the people of both of Northern Ireland's traditions want to take the path of peace and reconciliation, not hatred and violence."

The killing was the first since the IRA bombed a British army base last October killing one soldier and injuring 30 and it put a further strain on a ceasefire by the IRA's Protestant Loyalist foes. The IRA ended its own ceasefire a year ago.
"The loyalists and their leaders have shown great courage and restraint in not allowing themselves to be drawn into an escalating spiral of violence. I urge them to remain steadfast," Clinton said.

He said peace talks in Belfast, chaired by special U.S. envoy George Mitchell, still had his full support. "I urge all those taking part, who share a commitment to democratic values, to move as rapidly as possible into substantive negotiation about the future of Northern Ireland," Clinton said.
